intro: Talk about getting along, relationships and shared actions with reciprocal pronouns.
p.salir con: to go out with; to date
p.salir con.nota: Here it refers to dating; it can also mean going out socially with someone.
p.romper con.nota: In this lesson, it refers to ending a romantic relationship.
p.ligar: to flirt; to chat someone up
p.ligar.nota: Colloquial; the precise sense varies with context and region.
p.discutir.nota: It means “argue” in a quarrel; it can also mean “discuss” a subject or issue.
p.la pareja.nota: Grammatically feminine even when it refers to a male partner; it can mean one partner or a couple.
p.convivir.nota: Living with someone does not necessarily mean being a romantic couple.
p.el colega.nota: Colloquial; it can mean a friend or a work colleague, depending on context and region.
p.conocerse: to meet, to get to know each other
p.casarse con: to marry; to get married to
b1.texto:
With a plural subject, **nos**, **os** or **se** can show that people act on one another: **Nos conocimos** en la universidad; **Se abrazaron**. A reflexive action is different: **Ana y Luis se vistieron** means that each got dressed. Context helps distinguish the two readings.

**Nos** goes with **nosotros/as**; **os** goes with familiar **vosotros/as**, used in much of Spain; **se** can go with **ellos/as** or **ustedes**. In most of Latin America, speakers use **ustedes** with **se** and a plural verb: **Ustedes se conocieron**.

**Relationship vocabulary.** These expressions describe different experiences, not a fixed sequence or expected milestones: **conocerse**, **ligar**, **salir con** alguien, **enamorarse de** alguien, **convivir** or **vivir juntos**, **casarse con**, **discutir**, **romper con**, **hacer las paces**. Relationships differ; not everyone does all of these.

**Llevar + time expression + gerund** describes how long an ongoing activity has lasted: **Llevan cinco años saliendo**; **llevamos dos años viviendo juntos**. **Echar de menos** means to miss someone or something: **te echo de menos**.

In a quarrel, **discutir** means to argue; it can also mean to discuss a topic or issue.
b2.f0: How did you and Ana meet?
b2.f1: At a party. At first we got on terribly.
b2.f2: Really? But you have been dating for five years.
b2.f3: Yeah. We argue a lot, but we always make up.
b2.f4: And aren't you planning to live together?
b2.f5: Yes, in the summer. When Ana is away, I miss her a lot.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Se can go with ellos/ellas or ustedes; the subject here is nosotros.
b5.pregunta: Complete: she broke up with her boyfriend.
b5.o0.refuerzo: Romper con means to break up with someone, so con is the right preposition.
b6.o1.explicacion: Echar de menos is to miss.
b6.o2.explicacion: Echar de menos is to miss.
b7.pregunta: In «Ayer discutieron mucho y acabaron enfadados», «discutir» means that they…
b7.o1.refuerzo: That would mean they examined a topic; this context describes a quarrel.
b8.pregunta: Complete: they have been going out for two years.
b8.o1.refuerzo: After llevar and a time, the gerund.
b8.o2.refuerzo: After llevar and a time, the gerund.
b9.traduccion: We argue a lot, but we always make up.
b10.pregunta: In a greeting scene, «Ana y Luis se abrazan» means that they…
b10.o1.refuerzo: That would be a reflexive reading.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The pronoun se refers back to the subject.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about your relationships: who you get on with, who you argue with and how you make up.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud how you met an important person in your life and how the relationship has changed.
b6.o0.explicacion: Te echo de menos means I miss you, from echar de menos.
